data.title: More Than 22,000 Customers Affected as Hackers Leak Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Marketing Records
data.description:
Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase have disclosed a customer data breach after hackers targeted third-party service providers connected to their businesses, exposing thousands of records linked to marketing and customer benefits programmes.

The incident, claimed by ransomware group n0n, has potentially affected more than 22,000 customers, including around 16,000 JPMorgan Reserve cardholders and more than 6,000 premium Visa customers.

🚨 The n0n ransomware group leaked data belonging to thousands of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase customers, adding to a series of technology incidents that have raised consumer concerns. pic.twitter.com/hwahpgAiC4

— Dark Web Informer (@DarkWebInformer) November 19, 2026

Although the stolen information includes customer contact details, all three companies said their internal networks and payment systems were not compromised.

Hackers Target Third-Party Providers Behind Major Payment Firms

Rather than breaking directly into the systems of Visa, Mastercard or JPMorgan Chase, the attackers gained access through external service providers that handled customer-related information for the financial companies.

The ransomware group n0n claimed responsibility for the breaches, reportedly using compromised or stolen login credentials to enter the vendors' systems and extract databases containing marketing, loyalty and benefits programme records.

According to cybersecurity researchers, the group first appeared on its Tor-based extortion website on 9 November under the generic listing "Company #150".

By 16 November, it had identified Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan as affected companies and issued a 48-hour ransom deadline.

After the deadline expired on 19 November 2026, the group published the stolen spreadsheets online.

🚨 **BREAKING | 🇺🇸 MAJOR DATA BREACH CLAIMS ROCK GLOBAL FINANCIAL GIANTS!**

The 48-hour ransom deadline has expired, and hacker group **n0n claims to have leaked customer data linked to JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard.**

The alleged dump includes:
- 16,000 JPMorgan Reserve… pic.twitter.com/WOhvDM5jZJ

— @VijayBharat (@shikhar711) November 20, 2026

The group reportedly claimed to have obtained "hundreds of thousands of campaign interactions for tens of thousands of distinct cardmember email addresses".

Cybersecurity firm ZeroFox Intelligence has described n0n as a relatively new threat actor, with its first known appearance in September 2026.

Since then, it has reportedly carried out an average of two cyberattacks per day, placing it among the firm's five most active threat actors globally.

The group is also associated with double extortion, a tactic in which attackers demand payment both to restore access to compromised files and to prevent stolen information from being published.

More Than 22,000 Customers May Have Had Their Data Exposed

The leaked records vary across the three companies, but the exposure appears to be concentrated on customer information used for marketing and benefits programmes rather than financial transactions.

Around 16,000 JPMorgan Reserve cardholders may have had their names and email addresses exposed.

More than 6,000 premium Visa customers were also affected through a third-party service provider operating in the Asia-Pacific region.

FACT: The Visa, Mastercard & JPMorgan data leak gets funnier the deeper you dig 💀

▸ Hackers reportedly spent $7,216 on AI tools, then left their own server exposed with 1,719 files.

▸ @Mastercard 's leaked sample? Just 280KB with ~2,000 messy records.

▸ Over 6,000 @Visa… https://t.co/usKqS2H01Zpic.twitter.com/U1SxpMBZuJ

— FattDeFi (@0xFattDeFi) November 19, 2026

Mastercard separately confirmed that a limited amount of information belonging to customers enrolled in a specific benefits programme had been exposed, including email addresses.

The companies have stressed that the incident did not expose payment information such as card numbers.

There is also no indication that the attackers accessed the financial firms' core payment networks or directly compromised their internal systems.

The exposure nevertheless gives attackers access to customer contact information that could potentially be used for targeted phishing attempts, impersonation and other fraud.

🚨 Ransom group "n0n" posted 59 victims today (Nov 16, 2026)

Top names:
- Mastercard: cardmember names, emails and mobile numbers from Middle East and Africa programs, plus premium travel and dining bookings
- Visa: the same cardmember data for Asia Pacific markets
- JPMorgan… pic.twitter.com/zon6pVvXvb

— Ransom-DB (@Ransom_DB) November 16, 2026

How Have Visa, Mastercard And JPMorgan Responded?

JPMorgan confirmed that external service providers had been targeted and said the attackers likely accessed marketing information held by those vendors.

A bank spokesperson told Reuters,

"Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses."

The bank also said there had been no disruption to customer services and that affected customers would receive support, including complimentary credit monitoring.

We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack.

Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.… pic.twitter.com/08KZMusYFw

— Ares, Information Service (@Aresinfoservice) November 20, 2026

Visa confirmed that the incident involved a third-party provider in the Asia-Pacific region, while maintaining that its own systems were not affected.

A company spokesperson said,

"Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected."

Mastercard similarly acknowledged the exposure but said the information was limited to a small group of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefits programme.

The company added that its payment network remained unaffected and that the incident had been contained.

None of the three financial companies identified the breached service providers involved in the incident.

Visa says the attack originated with a vendor in the Asia-Pacific region, while all three financial giants say their core payment networks and card numbers were not compromised.

A group called n0n claimed responsibility for the leak.

— HERVY (@kanyankoleh) November 20, 2026

JPMorgan Separates Data Breach From Earlier Banking Outage

The latest disclosure has added to a difficult week for financial and technology services, following a series of disruptions that affected access to essential systems.

Earlier in the week, some JPMorgan customers experienced problems accessing their accounts and sending payments.

The bank attributed the disruption to a software update and stressed that it was unrelated to the data breach.

JPMorgan told The Wall Street Journal,

"There is no connection to service disruption of some customers experienced earlier this week."

The incidents came alongside the temporary grounding of flights by the Federal Aviation Administration and an earlier Microsoft outage that prevented users from accessing email services.

Together, the disruptions have raised concerns about the reliability of the technology infrastructure supporting everyday activities, from banking and communications to air travel.

For the financial industry, the latest breach also exposes a security weakness beyond the systems directly operated by major institutions.

Even when payment networks remain secure, external companies holding customer information can provide attackers with another route to sensitive data.

The risk is increasingly relevant to the cryptocurrency sector as Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan expand their involvement in digital assets and stablecoins.

With traditional financial institutions becoming more connected to the onchain economy, the security of their third-party partners is also becoming an important part of protecting customers and financial services.

data.title: What happened during Black Friday, when global markets plummeted?
data.description:
Author: Long Yue, Wall Street Insights

The story of Anthropic's first day of trading, which should have been a moment to solidify faith in AI, unexpectedly turned into a stress test.

On November 19th, Anthropic was priced at $83 and immediately surged to $111.50 at the open, causing a frenzy in the market. However, Anthropic's opening high was followed by a steady decline in stock price, closing at $97, with the gain narrowing to 17%.

The US stock market also saw a surge followed by a decline—the Nasdaq opened more than 2% higher but closed down 2.25%, with a single-day swing of over 4%. The S&P 500 lost approximately $1.3 trillion in market capitalization that day, closely matching the size of Anthropic's IPO fundraising. In the Asia-Pacific markets, Friday's opening saw a sharp drop, with the MSCI Asia Pacific Equity Index falling 1.7%, marking its seventh consecutive day of decline and approaching its lowest closing level since April. This also dragged down the MSCI World Index, pushing it towards its longest losing streak since September 2023. SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics of South Korea plunged 7% and 6% respectively, dragging down the South Korean KOSPI index by 4.7%. Japanese stocks suffered even steeper declines, with the Nikkei 225 index falling 4.6%, SoftBank Group plummeting 15%, chip testing equipment manufacturer Advantest crashing over 9%, and Tokyo Electron declining 7%. The three major A-share indices also fell in early trading, with the ChiNext index down nearly 3% and the Hang Seng Index down over 3%. Meanwhile, commodities and gold also suffered sell-offs. Spot gold fell about 1% on Friday to around $3,590 per ounce, with a cumulative weekly decline of over 7%.

What happened?

Opening: Everything looks great

On Thursday, November 19th, before the US stock market opened, a long-lost atmosphere of optimism permeated the market.

Anthropic listed at $83, higher than the upper limit of its previous roadshow range, corresponding to a valuation of approximately $1.1 trillion, setting a new record for the largest IPO in history. The news boosted US stock futures across the board overnight. At 9:30 AM Eastern Time, the Nasdaq Composite Index immediately surged more than 2%, and the S&P 500 also rose, with market sentiment briefly surging. At that time, the market generally interpreted this largest tech IPO in history as a strong signal that AI trading remains healthy. Jake Behan, Head of Capital Markets at Direxion, stated, “The market has been debating whether AI trading has gone too far, so seeing Nvidia exceed expectations and traders willing to chase Anthropic above its IPO price is a very noteworthy signal.” He added, “This doesn’t end all the valuation debate, but it strongly suggests that the market isn’t ready to give up on this deal.” However, the good times didn’t last.

Opening at a high point

Shortly after the market opened, a report from Bloomberg and other media outlets quickly spread across Wall Street trading desks:“Anthropic IPO reportedly allocated almost no shares to most institutional buyers.”

This news instantly alerted the market. ZeroHedge analysis suggests two possible interpretations: Either the underwriters were extremely confident in demand and deliberately reduced institutional allocations to ensure a post-IPO surge in stock price; or, institutions were simply unwilling to buy at $83, ultimately leaving the shares to less price-sensitive retail investors. The market seems to favor the latter. Morning to Noon: AMD Plunge, Chip Sector Suffers Just as the market was teetering on the brink of collapse, another bombshell dropped. Short-selling firm Hunterbrook released a report disclosing that it had shorted AMD, accusing the company of continuously providing chip firmware update services to companies blacklisted by the United States, and of having connections with some of the companies that previously sparked regulatory controversy surrounding Nvidia. AMD immediately responded, stating, "These claims distort AMD's business practices and partnerships." However, the statement failed to halt the decline. AMD's stock price fell by over 9% in a single day, dragging down the entire chip and AI sector. At noon, Anthropic was immediately sold off upon opening. At 12:00 PM Eastern Time, Anthropic officially opened at $111.50, a surge of over 34% from its IPO price of $83. However, the stock was immediately sold off – the logic of "profit-taking" kicked in. At the same time, the broader market also fell to its intraday low almost simultaneously. According to The New York Times, this trend mirrors SpaceX's IPO in June, which also saw an initial surge followed by a rapid decline, something investors were already prepared for. Anthropic ultimately closed at $97 per share, with gains narrowing to 17%. Afternoon: Decline Accelerates, All Sectors Collapse

Afternoon: Decline Accelerates, All Sectors Collapse

In the Eastern US afternoon, the decline further spread.

The Nasdaq opened more than 2% higher, but reversed course to close down 2.25%, with a single-day swing of more than 4 percentage points. The S&P 500 closed down 2%, with all 11 sectors in the red, and its market capitalization evaporated by about $1.3 trillion in a single day—almost equivalent to the valuation of about $1.3 trillion when Anthropic went public.

This sell-off isn't just a tech stock problem. All components of the S&P 500 Consumer Discretionary Index fell in the afternoon, led by Williams-Sonoma, which reported third-quarter sales that missed analysts' expectations. Strong consumer spending has been a key pillar of the U.S. economic resilience this year, and investors are particularly sensitive to signs of a slowdown in consumption. On that day, the VIX volatility index for US stocks rose to nearly 28, the VVIX (volatility of volatility) broke through 125, and the one-month implied correlation of the S&P 500 also climbed—analysts say these indicators all point to a broad-based risk-averse environment, rather than isolated sell-offs at the individual stock level. This also marks the sixth consecutive trading day of decline for the S&P 500, the longest losing streak since April 2024.

Behind the scenes, there are also negative Gamma and liquidity withdrawal

This crash has several hidden clues.

First, the technical structure is extremely fragile.

First, the technical structure is extremely fragile.

Nomura Securities strategist Charlie McElligott had previously warned that, amid the "four risks" of Nvidia's earnings report, Anthropic's IPO, and options expiration, market makers' negative Gamma exposure had risen to its highest level since 2019. When market makers are in a negative Gamma state, they are forced to hedge—selling when the market falls, further amplifying the decline. The large influx of 0DTE (zero-day expiration) options in the afternoon further eroded the support for longer-term options. Secondly, the IPO itself "drained" market liquidity. This IPO raised a total of $81.3 billion (including $26.7 billion in vendor placement, totaling over $100 billion). Trading desk sources indicate that market participants sold gold, copper, cryptocurrencies, and AI-related assets such as Nvidia to raise subscription funds. This aligns with market activity: gold fell below $3,800, copper prices plummeted by about 5%, and cryptocurrencies saw a broad-based correction. Third, the consumer sector's drag was even more pronounced. All S&P 500 consumer discretionary stocks declined in the afternoon. Strong consumer spending has been a core pillar of the US economic resilience this year, and this signal has fueled investor concerns about a slowdown in consumption. Fourth, year-end profit-taking pressure. Meanwhile, institutional investors also have their own calculations. The New York Times points out that despite recent market volatility, investors have generally enjoyed substantial returns this year. Around Thanksgiving, traders tend to lock in profits because market liquidity tends to shrink at the end of the year, making it more difficult to trade at ideal prices. Optimists haven't given up yet. Goldman Sachs analyst Rich Privorotsky issued a warning early that morning, saying, "Today feels very important." He pointed out that institutional net holdings of tech stocks are around 18%, far lower than the index's 29% weighting, placing them near a five-year low – meaning that unless the market experiences a significant decline, a short squeeze could be triggered. Direxion also stated that the market remains generally positive about the Anthropic IPO; Nvidia's better-than-expected earnings and Anthropic's successful listing together provide confidence that "AI trading is not over." As for the future, market attention turns to the November 20th monthly options expiration date – with the concentrated expiration of negative Gamma positions, that will be the next key observation window.

data.title: Anthropic's IPO: Biggest loser missing out on 246.7 billion?
data.description:
Author: Blockchain Knight; Source: X, @BlocKnight21

Last night, Anthropic officially listed on Nasdaq with an IPO price of $83. After opening, the stock price surged to $111.50, a gain of over 34%, and its market capitalization exceeded $2 trillion during trading.

Although it subsequently retreated somewhat, it ultimately still rose by about 17% from the IPO price. This IPO not only refreshed the market's valuation expectations for AI companies but also brought substantial returns to early investors.

However, behind this capital feast, there is a poignant story.

Back in 2021, FTX founder SBF had already invested in Anthropic. Now that the company has successfully gone public, FTX, due to bankruptcy liquidation, had to sell this investment prematurely, missing out on a potential return of tens of billions of dollars. In 2021, Anthropic was a relatively new company, and market attention on generative AI was far less intense than it is today. FTX's investment arm, Alameda Research, invested $500 million, acquiring approximately 13.56% of Anthropic's shares. This investment was diluted through multiple rounds of financing, reducing the stake to 7.84% by early 2024. The real turning point came in November 2022 when FTX filed for bankruptcy protection due to a liquidity crisis, and SBF's business empire rapidly collapsed. To repay customers and creditors, the bankruptcy administration began selling off assets, and Anthropic's shares were naturally lost. In 2024, the court approved FTX's sale of these shares. In March of the same year, FTX first sold approximately 29.46 million shares, obtaining $884 million, and then sold the remaining approximately 15.07 million shares, obtaining approximately $452 million. The two transactions totaled approximately $1.336 billion. For the bankrupt consortium, this was a considerable return on investment, but it also meant that FTX completely lost the opportunity to continue holding Anthropic. The problem is that at the time, no one expected Anthropic to grow to its current size. According to calculations, if FTX had not sold and had held onto the shares until its IPO, their value could have reached approximately $37 billion (approximately 246.7 billion yuan), nearly 74 times its initial $500 million investment. The investors who acquired these shares back then have now become the winners. Another noteworthy detail is Binance. In November 2022, after FTX experienced a crisis, CZ announced that Binance had signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire FTX.com, hoping to help it overcome its liquidity crisis. However, just one day later, Binance withdrew, citing poor due diligence results. If Binance had completed the rescue back then, and the transaction had covered the relevant investment assets, the Anthropic equity might have become a highly valuable investment. To some extent, Binance might have also benefited from the rapid growth of the AI ​​industry. However, the initial acquisition intention mainly targeted FTX.com, not the entire FTX Group. Whether Alameda's Anthropic shares would be included in the transaction remains uncertain. Another noteworthy point is that FTX wasn't lacking in investment acumen; long before the AI ​​boom truly arrived, it had already bet on a star company like Anthropic. Unfortunately, Anthropic is now in the spotlight, while FTX, the company that first bet on it, has long since collapsed—a twist of fate.

data.title: Trump Administration Turns To Blockchain Intelligence To Cut Off Overseas Scam Networks
data.description:
The Trump administration is stepping up its fight against overseas scam networks by launching a new Threat Disruption Center designed to track criminal operations, disrupt illicit money flows and prevent stolen funds from reaching foreign fraud networks.

🚨U.S. LAUNCHES NEW THREAT DISRUPTION CENTER TO HIT SCAM AND CRYPTO CRIME NETWORKS WITH TRM LABS TECH! U.S. authorities just stood up a dedicated Threat Disruption Center inside the Homeland Security Task Force’s National Coordination Center. It’s built to cut off the money flowing to overseas criminal groups running scams, cybercrime, and sextortion schemes against Americans. The center pulls together more than 30 federal agencies plus over 440 state and local partners so they can triage victim reports faster, map the networks behind them, and act before funds get laundered further. @trmlabs is the primary private-sector partner supplying the tech.

— Crypto Banter (@crypto_banter) November 19, 2026

Announced on Wednesday by the Homeland Security Task Force's National Coordination Center, the initiative will bring together more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners to identify scam operations and coordinate with banks and cryptocurrency platforms to stop fraudulent payments.

DHS and the DOJ launched the Threat Disruption Center — 30 federal agencies and 440 state and local partners working to cut off the money Americans lose to foreign scams. https://t.co/6tCF12DGfx https://t.co/kJ7sPaW7uU

— Profilo politics (@profilopolitics) November 19, 2026

The center will work alongside private-sector companies to identify criminal networks and intervene before scammers can launder stolen funds or target additional victims. Its launch follows a March 2026 executive order directing federal agencies to collaborate with private companies to combat online fraud and other cybercrime targeting Americans.

US Government Turns to TRM Labs to Track Scam Networks

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs has been selected as the center's primary private-sector partner, highlighting the growing role of blockchain analytics in helping authorities investigate cryptocurrency-related financial crimes.

Under the partnership, TRM Labs will provide Ardence, an investigative platform that the center will use to map scam networks and identify victims.

TRM Labs, a Galaxy Ventures portfolio company, is supporting the new Threat Disruption Center and putting AI-powered investigations to work against scams and cybercrime. Proud to back a team building where it counts.

— Galaxy (@galaxyhq) November 19, 2026

The initiative is designed to help authorities respond more quickly to reports of online fraud and trace the financial networks responsible for moving stolen funds. Heith Janke, operations director of the FBI's Criminal Branch

"Every hour between a victim's report and a response gives criminals more time to launder stolen funds and identify their next target."

TRM Labs co-founder and CEO Esteban Castano also highlighted the importance of intervening before scammers can extract additional payments from victims.

"Stepping in sooner changes everything: a warning before the next payment, a scam website removed before it victimizes another family, or stolen funds frozen while they can still be recovered."

The center will therefore focus on coordinating investigations and working with private-sector organizations to identify suspicious financial activity, disrupt criminal operations and help prevent further losses.

Online Fraud Cost Americans More Than $17.7 Billion in 2025

The launch comes as online fraud continues to inflict substantial financial losses on Americans, with FBI figures highlighting the scale of the problem.

The FBI received approximately 453,000 reports of online fraud in 2025, with reported losses exceeding $17.7 billion.

This FBI in just 21 months: • 2,800+ fraud arrests • 2,700 indictments • $2.3 BILLION+ recovered Operation Blackout: • 23 scam compounds taken down • 700 fraud websites dismantled • $17 BILLION+ seized The new Most Wanted Fraudsters list has already led to 6 captures in just 3 months, tied to roughly $2 BILLION in fraud.

— FBI Rapid Response (@FBI_Response) November 16, 2026

Meanwhile, the Justice Department estimated in September that overseas scam centers cost Americans approximately $10 billion annually through schemes involving cryptocurrency and online investment fraud.

These operations often rely on financial networks to move stolen money, making it increasingly important for authorities to identify suspicious transactions and trace funds before criminals can launder them.

Un deepfake d’Elon Musk promettait de doubler les cryptos envoyées pendant un faux direct Tesla. Coinbase a bloqué 4,7 millions de dollars. Comment l’arnaque a-t-elle convaincu ses victimes ? 🎥₿ https://t.co/mjwTXAG60I

— Clubic (@Clubic) November 19, 2026

By bringing together federal agencies, local law enforcement, banks and cryptocurrency platforms, the new Threat Disruption Center aims to strengthen the response to these operations and make it harder for overseas criminal networks to profit from online scams.

The partnership with TRM Labs also underscores how blockchain intelligence tools are becoming an increasingly important part of financial crime investigations, particularly as authorities look for ways to trace illicit cryptocurrency transactions and identify the networks behind them.

data.title: Anthropic's market capitalization once ranked sixth on its first day of trading; it is creating billionaires in large numbers.
data.description:
Source: Phoenix Network "Storm Eye"

On November 19th, US local time, Anthropic officially listed on Nasdaq, trading under the ticker symbol ANT.Opening at $111.50, up approximately 34.3% from its IPO price, it reached a high of $115.10 during the day, with the gain expanding to approximately 38.7%. Subsequently, it continuously gave back its gains, hitting a daily low below $92.80, with the gain narrowing to less than 12%.

Based on the opening price, the company's market capitalization once exceeded $2 trillion.

Based on this intraday market capitalization, Anthropic, founded just over five years ago, has already entered the top ten of the world's most valuable listed companies, ranking sixth after Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet (Google's parent company), and Amazon. Even at the close of trading, on a fully diluted basis, Anthropic's market capitalization is approximately $1.77 trillion, still placing it among the world's highest-valued companies. Record-breaking IPO: A Frenzy of Buying and Selling. Anthropic's initial offering plan, placed it among the top tier of global IPOs this year. According to the original plan, Anthropic would publicly offer 825 million Class A ordinary shares, with a price range of $70 to $78 per share, corresponding to a fundraising scale of $57.75 billion to $64.35 billion. No one anticipated such overwhelming market enthusiasm. According to CNBC and other media outlets, citing sources familiar with the matter, at the moment the order book closed, institutional investors' total subscription intentions reached approximately $400 billion, while individual investor demand approached $100 billion, bringing the total intended investment to nearly $500 billion. Faced with this overflowing demand, Anthropic quickly made two adjustments: First, the offering size of Class A common stock was expanded to approximately 980 million shares, a 19% increase from the initial plan; second, the offering price was raised directly above the initial range, ultimately settling at $83 per share. Following the adjustments, the initial public offering (IPO) raised approximately $81.3 billion, surpassing the $75 billion initial public offering (IPO) of SpaceX in June of this year, becoming the largest initial public offering (IPO) in US stock market history. In US stock market IPO practice, underwriters typically include a 30-day over-allotment option, commonly known as the greenshoe option. Anthropic's offering also included this option. If the underwriters fully exercise the greenshoe option, the fundraising size could increase by approximately $12.2 billion, bringing the total fundraising to $93.5 billion. Once fully exercised, this would surpass SpaceX's record of $85.7 billion after the greenshoe option was exercised, setting a new historical high for total fundraising in a US IPO. The entity that created all of this has been established for less than six years. At the end of 2020, siblings Dario Amodi and Daniela Amodi, along with five other core members of OpenAI, left the company. The reason for leaving is clear: they judged that OpenAI, in its rapid commercialization, was constantly diluting the importance of AI safety, and its technological roadmap was continuously tilted towards commercial gains. In early 2021, seven people founded Anthropic in San Francisco, and in just a few years, it has grown into one of the most watched AI companies in the world. Based on the IPO price of $83, the company's fully diluted valuation is approximately $1.5 trillion, a size close to that of Tesla, which has been around for over 20 years. The market has already begun to speculate on its future potential. If the stock price reaches $90, the valuation will be close to $1.63 trillion, roughly equivalent to Meta's current market capitalization; at $104, the valuation will be approximately $1.88 trillion, approaching TSMC; at $190, the valuation will reach approximately $3.43 trillion, close to Google; and if it reaches $282, the valuation may exceed $5 trillion, approaching Apple's level. A Wealth Frenzy: Hundreds of Employees Riding the Wave of Riches This epic IPO's most captivating aspect is the realization of wealth by its internal employees. The prospectus reveals that as of September 30th, employees held approximately $119 billion in stock options with a weighted average exercise price of only $2.91 per share. Of this, approximately $73 billion worth of options have already vested and can be exercised and realized upon meeting certain conditions. Employees who received stock options earlier incurred lower costs. Options granted in 2023 but not yet exercised had an average exercise price of only $0.52. Compared to the offering price of $83, the book value of early-stage equity has increased more than a hundredfold. The prospectus did not disclose the shareholding details of each employee, making it impossible for outsiders to accurately verify who held this enormous wealth. Two private equity market research institutions built models based on publicly available information and provided two sets of estimations. Sacra estimates that approximately 2,800 current and former employees hold attributable equity worth at least $1 million. Hill estimates that among non-founding employees, 598 individuals have equity worth potentially exceeding $100 million. Anthropic's seven co-founders have also become billionaires; after the IPO, each will have a net worth exceeding $10 billion. They each hold approximately 1.4% of the shares (on a fully diluted basis), with no absolute controlling shareholder. It's important to clarify that these are just figures projected from the model. The actual earnings employees receive will be subject to deductions for exercise costs and taxes, potentially reducing their real income. Many people subconsciously assume that huge equity bonuses only flow to algorithm and model development positions, but job postings send a different signal. Reuters reviewed a 2024 administrative job posting with an annual salary range of $140,000 to $190,000, explicitly listing equity as a key component of the compensation structure. This means that as long as employees enter the market early enough, those in back-office support roles such as administration and operations can also share in this round of equity appreciation dividends. However, the window for distributing these dividends has a clear time boundary. Over the past year, Anthropic has embarked on a period of rapid expansion. At the end of 2024, the company had approximately 940 employees. By the end of September this year, the number had grown to 5,300, more than five times the original number. The cost of exercising stock options for later-joining employees has continued to rise. Those who truly reap substantial paper profits are still the earliest employees who joined the company at its inception. Beneath the spotlight, the growth narrative hides numerous hidden reefs. Capital is willing to give it a valuation in the trillions, but the key factor is still its revenue growth. According to the prospectus, Anthropic only received $41 million in revenue in 2023, reached $386 million in 2024, and is projected to rise to $4.585 billion in 2025. Fast forward to the first nine months of 2026, and revenue has already reached $33.242 billion, more than ten times the previous year. Looking at the quarterly figures, Q1 2026 revenue was $4.731 billion, Q2 was $11.555 billion, and Q3 continued to grow to $16.956 billion, with the growth momentum remaining consistent. The number of paying customers is also expanding accordingly. Over the past 12 months, Anthropic has had 11,900 enterprise clients contributing over $100,000 in revenue annually, but this number is projected to drop to just over 1,500 by the end of 2025. Claude Code, a code-based intelligent agent geared towards developers, has driven a significant amount of usage and is the main driver of revenue growth. However, this rapid growth has not yet led to Anthropic's profitability. In the first half of 2026, Anthropic's net loss reached $80.748 billion, far exceeding its revenue during the same period. According to the prospectus, in the first half of 2026, Anthropic recognized a loss of $72.388 billion due to changes in the fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and Simple Agreements for Future Equity (SAFE), accounting for nearly 90% of its net loss during the same period. Anthropic explained that these changes were primarily related to an increase in the fair value of outstanding convertible notes due to an increase in the company's valuation. Even excluding these, the operating loss for the first half of 2026 was still $693 million. The customer structure also presents potential risks. According to the prospectus, in the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic's top five customers contributed approximately 25% of its revenue. If these top customers cut budgets or switch to other companies, the growth curve will be immediately affected. Moreover, the competition in the AI ​​field is far from over. OpenAI and Google are continuously iterating their large models. No one can give a definite answer as to how long Anthropic's current technological advantage can be maintained. Today's lead could easily be overturned in a few months. Even more fundamentally challenging than model competition is computing power infrastructure. To reduce its dependence on cloud vendors, Anthropic is shifting towards building its own computing power clusters and signing long-term, irrevocable long-term commitments to computing power and infrastructure, with payment periods extending to 2045. Currently, the expansion of the US power grid is far behind the pace of computing power expansion. Projects are often delayed due to grid connection approvals and community resistance, with some sites relying on natural gas for self-generation to circumvent bottlenecks. Once subsequent chip architectures iterate rapidly and computing power prices fall, this fixed expenditure will create a mismatch with variable revenue, becoming a heavy burden on long-term profitability. On the eve of the IPO, Amodi and JPMorgan Chase CEO Dimon had a public dialogue.

Amodi and JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon in conversation

In the conversation, Amodi reiterated a piece of advice from someone else: Don't let your company's valuation be one dollar higher than its true value.

This statement perfectly aligns with the core principles that Anthropic repeatedly emphasized from its inception: restraint, a focus on security, and a rejection of empty grand narratives.

However, the sentiment of the capital market will not follow the cautious pace of management. Capital prematurely realizes its expectations in stock prices, but all stories must eventually be tested.

data.title: I won't applaud Anthropic's IPO.
data.description:
At 9:30 AM Eastern Time on November 19th, the Nasdaq bell rang for a company founded just five years prior—AI giant Anthropic (ticker symbol ANT) officially went public. The global trillion-dollar market capitalization club welcomed a new member, and it's Made in the USA. As a benchmark company in the global AI field, Anthropic created the largest IPO in human capital market history—raising approximately $107.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX's record of $86.2 billion set just this year. This is a landmark moment, but the celebration may only belong to a select few: with Anthropic's public listing, a large number of new millionaires will be created. The company has approximately 5,300 employees, more than half of whom will hold shares worth over $10 million, and over 600 will hold shares worth over $100 million. However, it won't be easy for retail investors to get a piece of the pie in the secondary market. As the AI ​​wave continues, mega-corporations are entering the capital market at a record pace, and their need for funding is becoming increasingly urgent. OpenAI is expected to list on the US stock market in 2027, and other medium-sized and large AI companies will also seek IPOs. From this perspective, isn't the US stock market also a financing market? It's just that the US stock market is dominated by institutions and has the world's broadest liquidity support. Anthropic's IPO is a landmark event in the development of AI, but it also carries a less than positive signal. Anthropic's revenue in Q4 2025 was $2.04 billion, a 48% quarter-over-quarter increase; Q1 2026 revenue was $4.731 billion, a 132% quarter-over-quarter increase; Q2 2026 revenue was $11.555 billion, a 144% quarter-over-quarter increase; however, Q3 2026 revenue was $16.956 billion, with the quarter-over-quarter growth rate dropping to 46.7%. According to the latest data, as of October 31, 2026, the company's disclosed annualized revenue (Run-Rate Revenue) is approximately $81 billion, an increase of approximately $10 billion from approximately $71 billion at the end of September (a month-over-month increase of approximately 14%).

I. Growth Shift, Urgency for IPO

III. The Drainage Effect: A Signal of the End of the Bull Market?

Historically, almost every bull market has seen massive financing events, which can signal the end of the bull market. SpaceX raised $86.2 billion in its IPO, Anthropic raised $107.3 billion, and OpenAI's IPO is expected to raise over $50 billion. These three mega-IPOs alone will drain approximately $240 billion of market liquidity. This does not include other companies' IPOs or funds withdrawn from the market through equity and debt financing.

data.title: The third "bottoming out"
data.description: Bitcoin experienced a "Black Friday," falling below 62k this morning, reaching a low of 61.4k. Looking at the year 2026, both the daily and weekly charts show three very clear tests of the 60k "bottom area" (temporarily). The first was in early February this year, the second in early July, and the third this morning (or this week, mid-to-late November). The intervals are very even, approximately five months each; although the aftershocks of the July wave dragged on until mid-August, the real low point still occurred at the beginning of the month. The three extreme levels of the pullback reached 59.8k, 57.8k, and 61.4k (temporarily). These three "bottoming out" all landed near the $60,000 mark. The first two even broke through it, but the methods of testing each time were different: The one in early February was a rapid spike. On February 6th, Bitcoin plummeted from $67.5k, reaching a low of $59.8k (touching the $50,000 range), but then recovered to $68.6k that same day. The lower shadow was extremely long, like a needle piercing and then pulling out, leaving only a single point. That attack was leveraged; a single spike caused positions that were destined to be liquidated to be wiped out. The one in early July was a test of patience. From early June to mid-August, more than two months of back-and-forth trading at low levels gradually tormented those holding positions. On July 1st, the price bottomed out at $57.8k. There were no sudden gasps of alarm, only a growing, increasingly agonizing anxiety. Eventually, the initial momentum wore thin, and hesitation set in, fearing a further drop to $40,000. From the 15th (last weekend), the price continued to decline from its lows, reaching a low of 61.4k this morning. It seemed the bulls were utterly powerless. There was no rapid rebound after a sharp drop, no back-and-forth bottoming, just a relentless, rapid, step-by-step decline. Since breaking below the 200-day moving average (73k) on November 11th, there have been nine consecutive days of decline (today's close is not yet in sight), and the weekly chart is now showing its sixth consecutive bearish candle, with each intraday rebound becoming weaker than the last. Yet, within this seemingly hopeless landscape of bearish candles, a glimmer of hope appeared. The Zuo Zhuan states: "In battle, courage is paramount. One should strike with full force at the first drumbeat, but the momentum wanes at the second, and is exhausted at the third." The bears' battles likely follow a similar pattern. The first plunge from 126k to 59.8k was the most powerful. The second plunge, five months later, only reached 57.8k, a back-and-forth struggle that expended considerable energy. This latest counterattack, breaking through the 200-day moving average and launching a fierce downward attack, has forced the bulls into retreat, but it may be their last gamble. This final all-out attack—it's all or nothing. Things rarely happen more than three times. Three battles and they're exhausted. Three strikes and they're out. This is a philosophical way of thinking, but it doesn't necessarily guarantee the accuracy of every micro-observation. On July 22, 2021, when Bitcoin was at 32k, I wrote an article titled "The Short Sellers Striked Out." The situation then was somewhat similar to today: a drop to 29k on May 19th, a bottoming out at 28.8k on June 22nd, and a pullback to 29.3k on July 20th. The short sellers exerted extreme pressure three times, and each time they were thwarted. The article concluded that the short sellers had collapsed. Two months later, Bitcoin returned to 50k; four months later, it reached 69k. A year later, in May 2022, when Bitcoin was at 36k, I wrote another article, "Market Observation: BTC's Major and Minor Triple Bottoms." Three pullbacks, all landing on the same lower channel line; the article concluded by speculating that this was likely the final bottoming process. Six months later, the market fell to $15.5k. Returning to this year, today... The three bottoms all occurred around $60,000, indicating support at this level. This is a fortress, and the attackers failed to breach it after three attempts (strictly speaking, even a brief breach followed by a quick recovery counts as a breach). The first was buying during the price spike, the second was the gradual accumulation of shares during the bottoming process, and the third is still ongoing. The night before dawn is the darkest and coldest. The virus is most virulent and painful on the eve of recovery. The market on the eve of recovery is the most brutal and despairing. Ultimately, logic is not proof of a bottom. The true bottom can only be identified after the bear market has ended and we look back. "You can't see the true face of Mount Lu because you're in the mountain yourself." Now, standing halfway through, the three local lows we've seen could be the bottom of a valley, or they could be three steps on a mountainside. The former is the bottom. The latter is the path. However, the intervals between these three instances are remarkably even: early February, early July, and mid-November, roughly every five months. The market seems to be testing the waters rhythmically. With each test, some selling pressure is absorbed. This regularity doesn't resemble a rout. A rout is chaotic, a stampede, a precipitous collapse. An orderly decline, on the other hand, often indicates a change of hands in the market. "When you reach the end of the stream, sit and watch the clouds rise." The stream ends, the sound of water ceases, and it seems to have nowhere to go. As for when the clouds rise, and how high, one only needs to remain calm and "sit and watch." The journey of accumulating positions in the bear market should be nearing its end as planned. Sit leisurely on the bank and leave the waiting to time.

data.title: Anthropic shares surged 17% on their first day of trading, marking a significant milestone for the AI ​​industry.
data.description:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodi.

Author: Boyang, Tencent Technology

Anthropic's first day of trading on Nasdaq ended with a significant surge, but the intraday volatility also served as the first warning bell for this star AI company.

On November 19th, US local time, Anthropic stock debuted on Nasdaq with an offering price of $83, and the stock code is ANT.

On November 19th, US local time, Anthropic stock debuted on Nasdaq with an offering price of $83, and the stock code is ANT.

Due to concentrated buying pressure, the first trade didn't occur until 11:48 AM Eastern Time, at $111.50, 34.3% higher than the IPO price. The stock price subsequently fell steadily, reaching a low of $92.72. At the close, Anthropic closed at $97.17, up $14.17 from the IPO price, a gain of 17.07%. According to CNBC data, the trading volume reached 839.6 million shares, with a closing market capitalization of approximately $1.272 trillion. In after-hours trading, the stock price further declined, falling by more than 3%. This is the largest IPO in the history of the US capital market. Anthropic's IPO involved the offering of 980 million shares at a price of $83 per share, raising approximately $81.3 billion. Including a $26 billion private placement, the total fundraising exceeded $107 billion, surpassing SpaceX's record of approximately $75 billion set in June. 1200 institutions queued to subscribe, but more than half were unsuccessful. Demand for Anthropic's IPO far exceeded the offering size. The company initially set a price range of $70 to $78, but ultimately priced it at $83, higher than the upper limit. The number of shares offered was also increased by approximately 19% from the original plan, bringing the total public offering to approximately $81.34 billion. However, not all funds ultimately went into Anthropic's account. According to the final prospectus, the company issued 956,351,354 shares, approximately $79.38 billion. Another 23,648,646 shares were sold by existing shareholders, amounting to approximately $1.96 billion. In other words, the total IPO amount was approximately $81.34 billion, the vast majority of which came from newly issued shares, with a smaller portion from existing shareholders selling their holdings. In addition, Anthropic arranged a $26 billion private placement, with participation from investors including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, Micron, and TSMC. Combined, the total financing amounted to approximately $107.3 billion. Underwriters also have a 30-day over-allotment option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares. This deal involved more than 20 banks, with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs serving as lead underwriters. It surpassed SpaceX's previous IPO fundraising record and pushed the fundraising capabilities of AI model companies to a new level. However, not all institutions that wanted to buy shares received them. Bloomberg, citing sources familiar with the matter, reported that approximately 1,200 institutional investors participated in the subscription, with more than half ultimately receiving no allocation. The allocation clearly favored US investors, leaving many overseas institutions with unfulfilled orders. According to the Wall Street Journal, retail investors received approximately 15% of the offering, amounting to about $12 billion, lower than Anthropic's previously disclosed 20% cap. Despite the increased size of Anthropic's IPO, a significant number of institutions were unable to purchase shares, indicating that demand was not merely driven by a few large funds driving up prices, but rather reflected a broad range of funds seeking direct exposure to a leading AI company. However, the allocation results also sparked another form of discontent. Investor Rakesh Agrawal questioned whether the stock allocation in such a large offering seemed to favor priority clients, while founders, employees, and early investors may not have received shares commensurate with their contributions. Axios reporter Dan Primack, however, offered a different perspective, noting that venture capital-backed companies have now become trillion-dollar IPOs, signaling the end of the era of startups represented by the term "unicorn." The seven founders' net worth is nearly $140 billion, and employees are also big winners. The IPO gave a more tangible valuation to the wealth of Anthropic's seven founders. Based on the offering price, the shares held by the seven founders are worth approximately $139.3 billion. Of these, CEO Dario Amodei's shares are valued at approximately $20.07 billion, co-founder Tom Brown at approximately $20 billion, and Sam McCandlish at approximately $19.92 billion. The remaining four founders, Christopher Olah, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, and Daniela Amodei, also have shares valued at close to $20 billion. The seven founders each sold approximately 3.378 million shares in the IPO, cashing out approximately $280 million each based on the offering price, totaling approximately $1.96 billion. Their control over the company does not entirely depend on economic shareholding. The prospectus shows that the founders' LLC holds a special Class F share, possessing 50.1% of the company's total voting rights, but not economic interests. The seven founders were the entity's original sole members. Employees also share in the wealth growth resulting from the IPO. According to the prospectus, as of September 30, 2026, the book value of employee stock options is approximately $119.1 billion, of which approximately $72.6 billion has already vested. Independent research firm Sacra estimates that approximately 2,800 current and former employees hold at least $1 million in pre-tax vested equity. Hill, a private equity trading platform, estimates that 598 non-founding employees hold equity worth over $100 million. Beyond Claude Code, Anthropic is starting to offer discounts to attract enterprise clients. Before its IPO, Claude Code was Anthropic's most watched growth engine. After going public, the company is expanding its product line from programmers to other departments within enterprises. Anthropic has launched a series of products, including Claude Cowork for non-technical employees, Claude Managed Agents to help developers build and run AI agents, and Claude Security, Claude Design, and Claude Science. The company hopes Claude will evolve beyond a programming tool and integrate into more business areas such as sales, finance, human resources, marketing, and security. A software company executive revealed that their company's AI budget, previously over 90% allocated to engineering, is now around 60% for programming, with the remainder being allocated to Cowork, Design, and Security. Human resources and finance teams use Cowork to create financial forecasts, while the sales team uses it to generate market research reports. Customer adoption is expanding, but Anthropic is also offering greater price incentives to secure these budgets. Software procurement consultants and clients revealed that Anthropic is offering some companies product credits of up to $100,000 in exchange for higher annual spending commitments or to encourage clients to sign contracts by a specified date. Partners stated that clients can receive credits of up to $2,000 per user when trying products such as Cowork, Design, and Security. The discounts are also substantial. Managers from two clients stated that Anthropic is offering discounts exceeding 30%, with one contract offering a discount more than double that of a previous contract. One company provided a more concrete example: when the annual spending commitment was $1 million, Anthropic offered a discount of approximately 15% in the first quarter; increasing the commitment to $3 million brought the discount closer to 30%; and if the customer committed to spending over $5 million annually, the discount could further increase to over 30%. Some contracts also included share-of-wallet clauses, requiring customers to commit a certain percentage of their AI budget to Anthropic. In some cases, customers were also required to submit invoices and other documentation to prove they had fulfilled their commitment. NPI Financial analyst Madisyn Ellsworth stated that the company began noticing these clauses in early November. OpenAI also used similar arrangements, but NPI did not see OpenAI requiring customers to submit documentation to prove compliance. These practices reflect the changing landscape of competition in the enterprise AI market. Anthropic no longer just needs to prove Claude Code is usable; it also needs to win over customers to allocate more departments and budgets to Claude. For enterprises, discounts can lower the barrier to entry for trial use, but increased AI usage can also lead to uncontrolled spending. Some customers have begun monitoring high usage and even proactively cutting expenses. Competitors are also accelerating their efforts. OpenAI is entering the cybersecurity market, while Codex is vying for programming customers through price reductions; Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace have mature office software systems, and Anthropic's expansion into spreadsheets, collaboration, and office tools inevitably puts it in the territory of these two giants. Meanwhile, companies like FedEx, Robinhood, Coinbase, and Shopify are developing their own AI tools, hoping to flexibly switch between Anthropic, OpenAI, and open-source models. For model companies, while the frequency with which clients use AI is important, the ability to retain clients long-term and encourage them to continuously increase their budgets is equally crucial.

data.title: North Korean Hackers Move $101.9 Million Through Sky's Stablecoin Swap Facility Using Funds Linked to Bybit Hack
data.description:
Hackers Linked to North Korea Pushed Millions Through a Popular Stablecoin Swap Tool

A swap tool at the centre of the Sky stablecoin system, formerly known as MakerDAO, was used by wallets tied to North Korean hackers to move about $101.9 million, according to analysis by blockchain risk firm Inca Digital.

CoinDesk reported the findings on 19 November 2026.

Inca has not made its report public, and a second firm, Nominis, reviewed the data at CoinDesk's request.

The money passed through Sky's Peg Stability Module (PSM), which exchanges Circle's USDC for Sky's USDS or DAI at a one-for-one rate.

Some of the wallets were funded with crypto stolen from the Bybit exchange in February 2025.

We’re aware of the recent CoinDesk report on activity involving the Sky Protocol Peg Stability Module (PSM), predominantly via third-party permissionless platforms.

Reports like this are taken seriously across the Sky Ecosystem.

For scale: the PSM has processed over $968…

— Sky (@SkyEcosystem) November 19, 2026

How Did Stolen Bybit Funds Reach the Module?

North Korean hackers took around $1.5 billion from Bybit in the February 2025 theft.

Inca found that, in the 10 days that followed, wallets holding the stolen assets sent $91.5 million through the PSM.

Nearly $30 million of that moved after 26 February 2025, the day the FBI publicly blamed North Korea and named TraderTraitor, a unit of the Lazarus Group, as the group responsible.

The FBI's notice also asked DeFi services and others to block transactions with, or derived from, the hackers' addresses.

🗞️ Sky (@SkyEcosystem)'s stablecoin system lost more than $1.5 billion in a day after a report tied its swap to North Korean hackers — and Sky answered with its own numbers.

1. What Moved Today

More than $1.5 billion in USDC (USD Coin) left Sky's PSM (Peg Stability Module)…

— Bullish Crypto Life (@BullsCryptolife) November 19, 2026

Nominis carried out its own review of the Bybit trail.

It examined more than 560 transactions across over 320 addresses and confirmed the North Korean links.

Nominis CEO Snir Levi told CoinDesk,

"The window to act is short, before the funds are converted."

He added that hackers favour liquid, decentralised venues and assets "nobody can freeze".

Why Does the Module Appeal to Criminals?

The PSM works much like a vending machine.

A user puts in USDC and receives USDS or DAI, with no fees or slippage.

That makes it efficient for ordinary traders and illicit actors alike.

The difference lies in the tokens on each side.

Circle can freeze USDC held in a flagged wallet, whereas USDS and DAI cannot be frozen in the same way.

A thief holding stolen USDC can therefore swap it into a token that has no such switch.

The North Korea-linked flows were only part of a wider picture.

Inca counted $518 million moving through the module from 422 wallets connected to hackers, phishing operations, sanctioned entities and addresses blacklisted by Circle and Tether.

This included $26.1 million swapped by the FTX Accounts Drainer after the exchange collapsed in November 2022, and $49.5 million in USDC that the Infini exploiter converted to DAI on the day of the February 2025 hack.

NEW: @SkyEcosystem's $2.7B USDC reserve could face a freeze.

Inca Digital traced $518M in transactions through Sky’s stablecoin swap facility from wallets tied to illicit activity. Of that, $101.9M was linked to North Korean actors, including wallets funded by the 2025 Bybit… pic.twitter.com/Ag17Pq7fpA

— SolanaFloor (@SolanaFloor) November 19, 2026

About 95% of the flagged swaps were routed through aggregators such as 1inch, ParaSwap and MetaMask Swaps.

Elliptic estimates that North Korean actors may have stolen more than $1 billion in 2026 alone, with the September Bitget hack taking the total past that mark.

What Happens if Circle Freezes the Reserve?

The risk does not come from a freeze function in Sky's own code.

It sits with Circle, which can blacklist an address after a court order or a request from law enforcement.

The PSM keeps about $2.7 billion of USDC in a single Ethereum wallet set up through Coinbase Prime, and lawful deposits are mixed in with everything else.

Circle cannot freeze part of a wallet, so a blacklist would lock the entire balance and halt swaps in both directions.

NEWS: Inca Digital traced $518M in illicit-linked swaps through Sky's Peg Stability Module, including 101.9MtiedtoNorthKorea,perCoinDesk.

ThePSMletsanyoneswapfreezableUSDC 1:1 for DAIorUSDS.

About 2.7BofPSMUSDC sits in one wallet Circle could freeze. pic.twitter.com/n3G8uD1Vvk

— Bankless (@Bankless) November 19, 2026

That could put pressure on USDS, with about $4.6 billion in circulation, and DAI, with about $3.8 billion.

Circle has not blacklisted the wallet so far.

Analysts quoted by CoinDesk regard the scenario as unlikely.

Amey Dandawate of Bluechip Ratings, said,

"I think this is a low probability outcome, but it is not entirely hypothetical.”

The same debate surfaced in 2022 after the US sanctioned Tornado Cash, when Maker co-founder Rune Christensen discussed reducing DAI's reliance on USDC.

Who Is Responsible for Screening DeFi Transactions?

Lawyers interviewed by CoinDesk disagreed on where the duty lies.

Ari B. Good of Cogent said keeping admin keys, upgrade or pause powers "does not make it decentralized in the eyes of sanctions law".

Sanjeev Bhasker of K&L Gates said there is no single rule requiring DeFi protocols to screen transactions.

How Has Sky Responded to the Findings?

The Sky Frontier Foundation said it "takes any concern about illicit activity in DeFi seriously" and had reviewed the flagged transactions.

It said Inca's figures cover any wallet linked to illicit actors, so part of the total did not come from a known cyberattack.

According to the foundation, nearly all of the flagged value came through third-party aggregators rather than the spark.fi or sky.money websites, and most of it moved between 2021 and mid-2024.

The foundation also said the flagged trades made up less than 0.06% of the more than $930 billion the module has handled, and under 0.03% of the volume in its LitePSM.

"Keeping DeFi both open and safe is a challenge for the whole industry.”

The figures come from Inca Digital via CoinDesk: 422 wallets, $101.9M tied to North Korean actors. Sky called them alleged and put them at roughly 0.03% of $968B in PSM volume. It said the activity ran mainly through third-party platforms. pic.twitter.com/VknNX1VD6P

— CryptoNewsLive (@CryptoNwsOrg) November 19, 2026

A Coinbase spokesperson said customers control their self-custodial wallets and that the exchange works with law enforcement.

Galaxy Digital, which holds $100 million in Sky's interest-bearing sUSDS, did not respond to CoinDesk.

No new comment from Christensen was reported.

Does the Wider Financial Picture Add Pressure?

Sky's credit standing is already weak.

Moody's gave the protocol a B3 issuer rating in October in line with the B- grade S&P assigned in August 2025.

Rating Agencies Arrive in DeFi

• Moody's rated Sky Protocol B3, citing about $90M of equity against $10B of assets, and set equity above 2.5% of assets as the bar for an upgrade

• S&P launched a scorecard for DeFi lending vaults, a market that grew from $1.5B to $10B in two… pic.twitter.com/qtMaqlYael

— Edge Capital Management (@EdgeCapitalMgmt) October 13, 2026

Both are classed as junk.

Grove, an agent of Sky, has also extended Galaxy a $500 million credit line funded in USDS.

North Korea-linked theft remains a live concern across the industry.

Last week, US authorities moved to seize $1.2 billion stolen in the Binance hack.

The Inca and Nominis findings have not been published separately, and MLQ.ai said it could not verify them independently.

data.title: The largest IPO in history cooled down within an hour of opening.
data.description:
Authors: Li Dan, Li Jia, Wall Street Insights

AI unicorn Anthropic broke SpaceX's IPO fundraising record set five months ago, with its opening surge on the US stock market exceeding the highest expected level in the grey market, pushing the company's market value to over $2 trillion. However, the fervor quickly cooled down.

The stock price fell 13% from the opening price within half an hour of trading, marking the worst half-hour opening for a major US IPO since 2008.

On Thursday, November 19th, Eastern Time, Anthropic officially began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. It opened at $111.50, approximately 34.3% higher than its IPO price. During the session, it reached a high of $115.10, with the gain expanding to approximately 38.7%. However, it subsequently gave back its gains, falling to a daily low below $92.80, with the gain narrowing to less than 12%. By the close, it was up approximately 17.1% from its IPO price, essentially erasing half of its opening gains. In after-hours trading, it even fell below its closing price. The Anthropic IPO raised approximately $81.3 billion, breaking the global record for IPO fundraising. Investor enthusiasm for Anthropic provides an important indicator of the capital market for the AI ​​industry. The record-breaking fundraising on the first day of trading demonstrates that the capital market remains willing to provide substantial funding to leading AI companies. However, the rapid reversal of gains within half an hour of opening indicates that while the leading AI company's status generated strong initial demand, it did not alleviate investors' concerns about high valuations, massive computing power investments, and future profitability. The future performance of Anthropic will be an important window for observing the heat and sustainability of the entire AI investment cycle. Anthropic's record-breaking $81.3 billion IPO raised approximately $1.77 trillion at the close. On November 19th, Eastern Time, Anthropic officially began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. The company had previously set its offering price at $83 per share, higher than the guidance range of $70 to $78, raising approximately $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX's previous record of approximately $75 billion in IPO fundraising, becoming the largest IPO in history. In addition, Anthropic raised approximately $26 billion through a concurrent private placement, bringing the total transaction size to approximately $107.3 billion. It's important to distinguish this from the record-breaking IPO public offering of $81.3 billion, while the $107.3 billion includes the private placement. Based on the offering price of $83, Anthropic's valuation at the time of listing was approximately $1.5 trillion. Pre-IPO grey market trading released strong bullish signals. German brokerage Lang & Schwarz previously offered a price as high as $105, a 26% premium over the offering price; perpetual futures linked to Anthropic on the cryptocurrency platform Hyperliquid also significantly exceeded the offering price. After the market opened, Anthropic's stock price performance far exceeded the levels predicted in the grey market. Based on the opening price, the company's market capitalization briefly surpassed $2 trillion. At this intraday market capitalization, Anthropic, only five years old, entered the top ten of the world's most valuable listed companies, ranking after Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet (Google's parent company), and Amazon. In other words, Anthropic's opening market capitalization exceeded that of two of the "Magnificent 7" tech giants—Tesla and Meta—second only to the other five, and also surpassed SpaceX's opening valuation of approximately $1.96 trillion. However, Anthropic's stock price surge failed to hold, ultimately closing at $97.17. On a fully diluted basis, the company's valuation at the close was approximately $1.77 trillion. At the closing price, Anthropic's market capitalization failed to surpass SpaceX's first-day trading volume. Despite a significant pullback from its intraday high, Anthropic's closing valuation still places it among the world's highest-valued companies. Anthropic saw extremely high trading activity in its initial trading session. Yahoo Finance data shows that the first trade of $111.50 involved approximately 108 million shares, totaling about $12 billion; in the first full minute of trading after listing, the trading volume further reached approximately $15 billion. This trading volume far exceeds that of many previous large IPOs. Yahoo Finance calculated that Anthropic's initial trading volume exceeded SpaceX's approximately $9 billion in its first minute of trading in June of this year; the trading volume in the first full minute of trading was nearly twice that of SpaceX and about three times that of Alibaba's first minute of trading in 2014. However, the buying enthusiasm quickly turned into selling. Yahoo Finance, after comparing minute-level trading data from 21 large US IPOs, pointed out that Anthropic's performance in the first half hour after listing was the worst among large US IPOs since 2008. Specifically, Anthropic's stock price fell from its initial trading price of $111.50 to approximately $97, a drop of about 13% within half an hour. This performance was slightly less dramatic than the drop experienced by e-commerce company Coupang half an hour after its IPO; in contrast, SpaceX's stock price still rose nearly 10% half an hour after its IPO. The stock price subsequently continued to fluctuate downwards, reaching a low of $92.72 during the session, only about 11.7% higher than its IPO price of $83. Compared to the 34.3% increase at the opening, the stock price at one point almost completely erased its initial premium. At the close, the stock price rebounded to $97.17, but was still about 12.8% lower than the initial trading price of $111.50. In other words, while Anthropic ultimately closed with a 17.1% gain, it had given back about half of its opening 34.3% gain. Yahoo Finance also estimated that the decline in the first half hour of trading reduced the company's market capitalization by nearly $200 billion. This transaction also highlights the difference between the IPO's first-day price and its long-term valuation: the initial surge in the first trade and early opening reflected investors' enthusiasm for scarce AI assets, while the subsequent rapid decline showed that funds did not form a sustained and consistent buying intention at the high level.

The CEO rings the bell, pledging not to succumb to commercial and political pressure, emphasizing AI safety and medical breakthroughs

At the Nasdaq listing ceremony, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, company president and co-founder Daniela Amodei, and other co-founders and executives jointly rang the opening bell.
